scope: Corollary 2.2 (Buffered and shrinking-patch comparison) of the manuscript “Conformal universality of bulk Ising correlations under weak interactions” (preprints/Conformal-universality-of-bulk-Ising-correlations-under-weak-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8a815e7845436e07), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix c > 0. If I ⊂ BR(z) and J ⊂ B(1+c)R(z)c, their conditional density ratios in Lemma 2.1 lie in [C−1 c , Cc], uniformly in the mesh, common pins, and fields. There are C < ∞ and θ > 0 such that, if I ⊂ Bw(z), J ⊂ BR(z)c, and R ≥ 8w ≥ 8 in lattice units, the absolute log density ratio is at most C(w/R)θ . (2.3) No unpinned neighborhood of I is required. The buffered bound holds for fixed polygonal separating collars with positive relative width, and for their intersections with a free or fixed physical boundary. It also compares different continuations or volumes when the reference interaction agrees in the separating chart. The same assertions hold for mixtures and after a common conditional randomization of the local spins. Finitely many shrinking patches can be changed successively.
